data.why: The repo's own ingestion pipeline (python -m src.ingestion.make_samples then python -m src.ingestion.run --city boston), run during install, populates data/boston/*.parquet entirely from in-repo sources: real checked-in data for hospital_demand (data/ma_dph_respiratory.csv), events (data/boston_events.csv) and academic_calendar (data/boston_academic_calendar.csv), plus synthetic fallback samples (data/samples/*.csv) for transit, bikeshare, weather and wastewater since their live APIs (Open-Meteo, MBTA, Ticketmaster, WastewaterSCAN) are unreachable outside GitHub/PyPI during install and the app has no network at runtime. This is exactly the documented local-dev workflow (CLAUDE.md, docs/01-getting-started.md).

goals: Visualize eight aligned weekly/driver signals (transit, bikeshare, weather, events, academic calendar, wastewater per pathogen, hospital demand) on one shared timeline
Run lagged cross-correlation between a chosen driver signal and respiratory ED demand to find how many weeks the driver leads demand
Check whether a driver's best lag survives Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons, not just a raw p-value
Fit a surge-label logistic regression (AUC-ROC) and a count regression (Poisson vs. Negative-Binomial) of hospital demand on a lagged driver
Validate a fitted model out-of-sample with walk-forward (expanding-window) folds to check for overfitting
Inspect the driver-correlation matrix and variance inflation factors to catch confounded drivers before trusting an individual coefficient

review.summary: The tree follows the README's workflow closely: aligned timeline, lag scan with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and the ambiguity flag, surge and count fits, then walk-forward and VIF checks. Every screen I sampled matches its node. It needs small fixes before filing: the 'synthetic' data note is wrong, one action is misplaced, the Overview readout and the CSV export are missing as features, and check.json cites screens that don't line up with this folder.
